# 002 · A refactor believed equivalent that changes null handling

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✗ Violation: 1 of 36 cases changed** | functional, compatibility | medium | refactor, behaviour change not intended | [`OrderLifecycle#decide`](../../apps/boxoffice/ticketing-domain/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/ticketing/domain/OrderLifecycle.java) | [B8: Behavioural contracts](../../tools/contracts/README.md) |

> A nested switch was replaced by a one-line conditional. The agent that wrote it believed the two were equivalent, and every existing unit test passes. They differ on one input: a null status no longer throws.

## The change

Replace a five-line switch over the order status with `current == REFUND_PENDING ? ... : ...`, since only one status matters for a refund.

**Before** ([`OrderLifecycle.java`](../../apps/boxoffice/ticketing-domain/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/boxoffice/ticketing/domain/OrderLifecycle.java), line 44):

```java
};
case PaymentDeclined _ -> switch (current) {
    case PENDING_PAYMENT -> transition(DECLINED, RELEASE_SEATS);
    case CONFIRMED, DECLINED, REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED -> unchanged("payment outcome already recorded");
};
case PaymentRefunded _ -> switch (current) {
    case REFUND_PENDING -> transition(REFUNDED);
    case PENDING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, DECLINED, REFUNDED -> unchanged("no refund outstanding");
};
case CancellationRequested _ -> switch (current) {
    case CONFIRMED -> transition(REFUND_PENDING, RELEASE_SEATS, REQUEST_REFUND);
    case REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED -> unchanged("already cancelled");
    case PENDING_PAYMENT -> new Decision.Rejected("payment is in progress; try again shortly");
    case DECLINED -> new Decision.Rejected("the order was never paid");
```

**After:**

```java
};
case PaymentDeclined _ -> switch (current) {

    case CONFIRMED, DECLINED, REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED -> unchanged("payment outcome already recorded");
};
case PaymentRefunded _ ->
    current == REFUND_PENDING ? transition(REFUNDED) : unchanged("no refund outstanding");
case CancellationRequested _ -> switch (current) {
    case CONFIRMED -> transition(REFUND_PENDING, RELEASE_SEATS, REQUEST_REFUND);
    case REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED -> unchanged("already cancelled");
    case PENDING_PAYMENT -> new Decision.Rejected("payment is in progress; try again shortly");
    case DECLINED -> new Decision.Rejected("the order was never paid");
```

## What the verifier found

The behaviour changed for 1 of the 36 possible inputs. Each row is a concrete input that shows the difference:

| Input | The contract says | The code now does |
|---|---|---|
| `decide(null, PaymentRefunded[])` | `throws NullPointerException` | `Unchanged[reason="no refund outstanding"]` |

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

No: every existing unit test passes (`:ticketing-domain:test`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

`switch` on a null enum throws NullPointerException, while `==` quietly compares it as not equal. A caller that passes a null status, such as an order loaded from a corrupted document, now gets 'no refund outstanding' instead of failing fast. The bad state propagates instead of stopping at the first point that could have caught it. Changes like this pass review because the code is obviously simpler.

## Why the verdict is right

Null is part of the input domain for every reference parameter, because callers can pass it. The verifier executes decide(null, PaymentRefunded[]) on both versions: the contract records `throws NullPointerException`, and the new bytecode returns Unchanged. One case out of 36 differs.

## What to do

Keep the switch, or write the refactor with `default ->` (example 004), which preserves the null behaviour. If accepting null is intended, regenerate the contract so reviewers see that line change.

## Evidence

The proof trusted these JDK APIs to be pure: `java.lang.Enum.ordinal`, `java.lang.MatchException.<init>`, `java.lang.Record.<init>`, `java.lang.runtime.SwitchBootstraps.typeSwitch`, `java.util.List.copyOf`, `java.util.List.of`, `java.util.Objects.requireNonNull`.
